title: Freya and the Radiators
premise: After his mother's funeral, Casper Ishikawa finds in her effects a single untranslated sentence in a language he doesn't recognize, and a stranger named Freya who addresses his family by an old name no one has spoken in decades. Following Freya into the radiator-warmed basement of her boarding house, he discovers the community his mother secretly sustained for thirty years, and learns the sentence is a promise she made and broke to them. To translate it, Casper must reconstruct her silence from their memories, and in doing so chooses them over the family name that demands he sell the house. The book ends with Casper reading the translated sentence aloud at the boarding house table, becoming the heir to a promise rather than an estate.
about_author: Isandro Villalobos is a former hospital interpreter from Fresno who writes about the things families say in languages other than grief. Freya and the Radiators is his first novel.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At the reception after his mother's funeral, Casper performs flawless grief for relatives while cataloging her unexplained silences, including a locked cedar chest. A woman with chapped hands and a borrowed coat calls the family by the name 'Vasquez-Ishikawa' and leaves a brass radiator key in his palm. Emotional beat: the crack in his composure — the first conversation he cannot end with a smile.

chapters.title: Freya's Basement
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, intercut with Freya's. He follows the address on the key to a boarding house where immigrants gather around clanking radiators, and learns his mother funded it for decades under her first name. Freya shows him the chest's twin: a ledger of debts his mother forgave, ending in one untranslated sentence. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into betrayal — she had a whole life he was never allowed into.

chapters.title: What the Sentence Owed
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The boarding house faces eviction by Casper's uncle, who wields the family name and the funeral's legal machinery. Freya reveals the sentence is his mother's broken vow to shelter them 'until the last radiator cools' — and that she left before it was kept. Casper must choose between signing the sale papers and contesting the estate. Emotional beat: rising tension as duty and love become literally opposed signatures.

chapters.title: Until the Last Radiator Cools
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the estate hearing, Casper invokes a codicil hidden in the ledger, buying the house himself with his inheritance and estranging his uncle for good. That night he reads the sentence aloud, translated at last, and Freya's household sets another plate at the table. Emotional beat: resolution — Casper stops cataloging his mother's silence and starts answering it, heir to a promise instead of an estate.
